overview: This lesson introduces students to the anatomical structure of the human digestive system, focusing on identifying its major organs. Students will learn to distinguish between the primary organs of the alimentary canal and key accessory organs, and trace the sequential path food takes through the system.
objectives: [Remember] Identify the major organs of the human digestive system, including the oral cavity, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, and anus.
[Understand] Trace the sequential pathway of food through the alimentary canal from ingestion to egestion.
[Remember] Recognize and locate the key accessory organs of digestion: salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas.
[Apply] Position the identified organs correctly within the overall anatomical illustration of the digestive system.

activities.title: Where Does My Food Go?
activities.description: Initiate a class discussion by asking students what happens to food after they chew and swallow it, briefly introducing the concept of a system for processing food.

activities.title: Digestive System Puzzle
activities.description: Distribute an unlabeled diagram of the human digestive system. In pairs, students attempt to identify and label as many organs as they can based on prior knowledge or observation of the pathway shown.
materials: Printed unlabeled digestive system diagrams (one per student or pair)

activities.title: Anatomy Unveiled
activities.description: Using a projected or large chart of the digestive system, the teacher systematically labels and explains each major organ of the alimentary canal in sequence (from oral cavity to anus). The teacher then points out the accessory organs (salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, pancreas), emphasizing their relative positions and the food's pathway.
materials: Large labeled diagram of the human digestive system (digital or chart)

activities.title: Pathway Trace
activities.description: Students, using their own labeled or new blank diagrams, trace the complete food pathway with a coloured pen, mentally narrating the journey. The teacher circulates to provide support and clarify any doubts about the sequence or organ placement.

activities.title: Organ Match-Up
activities.description: Students complete a quick exit ticket or quiz where they match organ names to numbers on a new unlabeled diagram of the digestive system.
materials: Small exit tickets with an unlabeled diagram and corresponding organ names/blanks

assessment: An exit ticket where students label an unlabeled diagram of the digestive system with the names of the major and accessory organs, and indicate the direction of food flow using arrows.
